Biology Subdivisions of Biology Notes • The word ‘Science’ comes from the Latin word ‘scientia’, meaning ‘knowledge’. • Science is the systematic knowledge of the physical or material world gained through observation and experimentation. • Science has been classified into– (1) Natural Sciences and (2) Social Sciences. • The natural sciences comprise the physical sciences, Earth and space sciences, and life (biological) sciences; life sciences (biology) are further divided into many branches and sub-branches. • Lamarck and Treviranus introduced the term ‘biology’ independently in modern sense in 1802. Branches and Subbranches of Biology Zoology – Detailed study of the members of the animal kingdom and animal life in general. Botany – Detailed study of plants and their life. Palaeontology – The study of history of life on Earth as based on fossils. Fossils are preserved remains, impressions, or traces of plants, animals, and other organisms from the geologic past; they may be preserved in Earth’s crust and also by processes such as drying, freezing, and entrapment in amber or asphalt. Palaeobotany – Study of plant fossils. Ecology – The branch of biology that deals with the relation of organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.
